tecnicas.observacao: Template proposto pelo estudo a partir da categorização de perguntas reais do StackOverflow (Seção 4.1). Acrescenta ao prompt base a tarefa de aprendizado [X] e o conjunto de dados [Y] (contexto sobre a intenção do código) e o objetivo do reparo [Z] (instrução com objetivo explícito); mantém o código em [CODE] e remove a pergunta «Is the following program buggy?». O contraste com PT-B (mesmo benchmark, cinco requisições por consulta) é de pacote: PT-E difere de PT-B em mais de um ingrediente, e não há ablação de X, Y ou Z; o ganho não pode ser atribuído a um único ingrediente. Pacote só de prompting (não híbrido). Quando X, Y ou Z não estavam disponíveis, foram usadas variantes do template sem o elemento ausente (p. 6); o número de casos com cada variante e quem preencheu X/Y/Z não são informados.

citacoes.trecho: In particular, we split the debugging task into three steps, i.e., fault detection, fault localization, and program repair.
Prompt Template (Basic): Is the following program buggy? If so, please repair it. [CODE]
On top of the observation from real-world questions, we propose an enhanced prompt template (abbrev. PT-E) as follows:
Prompt Template (Enhanced): The following code is designed for a [X] problem trained on [Y].Please repair it in order to [Z]. [CODE]

where X describes the task (e.g., classification, regression), Y specifies the dataset (e.g., MNIST, ImageNet, numbers that follow the sine waves), and Z describes the objective (e.g., improve the accuracy) against the symptom.
Note that for the cases where the learning task/dataset/objective is unavailable, we use the variant templates as listed in Section 4.2.

In particular, for the cases that failed to be completely repaired in Section 4 (i.e., 18 cases), we first provide the fault locations using the following prompt template (Prompt Template (Locations), abbrev, PT-Loc).
(Round 3) Prompt Template (Locations) : The repair is wrong. Faults may happen in the following locations: [Loc]. Please repair it.
(Round 4) Prompt Template (IncR): The [Remaining_loc] is/are repaired incorrectly. Please repair it accordingly.
where the fault location information in PT-Loc is automatically filled in using the information provided by the benchmark [7], while the remaining locations in PT-IncR are filled after analysis.
We then integrate such failing information to ChatGPT by saying “The repair is wrong. For the input [1, 1], the output should be [0] instead of [1]. Please repair it again.”
It indicates that for DL program repair, providing the failing test cases may not be helpful.
We propose a few-shot prompt template as follows:
Compared with the human-written prompt (Reference), the meaning of two sentences are almost identical, which indicates the possibility to automate the prompt as discussed in RQ2.
We build a pipeline for our experiments using the latest ChatGPT API based on the gpt-3.5-turbo model released by OpenAI.
Due to the non-deterministic nature of ChatGPT, for each query, we run five independent requests by starting a new conversation every time on the API.
If the majority (≥ 3) of replies correctly report fault existence, we denote the result as a Yes; otherwise, No.
For ChatGPT, we put down the number of faults reported each round, and we use the best result among the five rounds for comparison.
To evaluate the automatic DL program repair ability of ChatGPT, we use a benchmark released by a recent study [7], which contains 58 buggy DL programs collected from StackOverflow and Github.
In the evaluation, we use the buggy programs collected from StackOverflow, because the programs in GitHub exceed the maximum input tokens.
While one should be careful with code refactoring and variable renaming, in case they cause a crash.
When asked to repair the program without an explicit repair goal, ChatGPT tends to focus on identifying outdated APIs and bad code smells.
It means that the repair could be invalid once newer version is released.
In addition, there are a few faults that are repaired correctly in the previous round but changed back to faulty in the next round.
Besides, ChatGPT is not able to execute the program at the current stage, even though a patch is provided by ChatGPT, a validation step is still needed.
Besides, ChatGPT’s replies are carried out manually, which may be subjective and misunderstandings.
To alleviate this threat, the cases used in the paper come along with StackOverflow post IDs.

Finally, since ChatGPT is trained on a large corpus of text data from the Internet (e.g., books, articles, open-source code repositories), it is possible that there is a data leakage problem, i.e., the cases in the benchmark were included in its training set, so the output is generated due to memorization.
This observation may partially alleviate the concern regarding such threat.
To avoid the difference between the ChatGPT website interface and the latest API, we repeat the experiment of RQ1 using the interface (Mar 14, 2023 Version).
One can avoid it by explicitly asking ChatGPT to return the complete repaired code.

Via further analysis, we found that among the 49 (72 - 23) escaped faults that belong to 18 cases, 16 of them (belonging to 7 cases) cannot be even detected, 32 of them (belonging to 11 cases) can be detected but cannot be correctly-localized.
With the best prior work, the performance of fault localization is still far less than satisfactory (only about 30%).

extracoes.metrica: Detection (programa com falha detectada: Y se a maioria, ≥ 3, de cinco respostas reporta corretamente a existência de falha)
extracoes.condicoes: Cinco requisições independentes por programa, cada uma em nova conversa; Y por maioria (≥ 3 de 5). Mesmo benchmark e mesmo modelo nas duas condições. PT-E difere de PT-B em vários ingredientes (acrescenta tarefa, conjunto de dados e objetivo; retira a pergunta «Is the following program buggy?»): contraste de pacote, sem atribuição a um ingrediente. Nos casos sem tarefa, dados ou objetivo disponíveis foram usadas variantes do template (número de casos nao_informado); quem preencheu X/Y/Z nao_informado. Temperatura e demais parâmetros de decodificação nao_informado. Observação do extrator: PT-E não pergunta se o programa tem defeito, e o estudo não descreve como a detecção foi julgada nessa condição. O baseline DeepFD (ferramenta sem LLM, fora do escopo) também detecta 34/34. Conferido na Tabela 2 (p. 4 do PDF), linha de totais e linhas por programa (soma das linhas Y de PT-B = 27, cálculo próprio), e no texto da p. 6.
